tool_input.description: Debug Japanese Imperial locale parse behavior
Remove debug file and re-run FastDateParserAgentTest

result:
I created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDateParserAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (no extension of `AbstractLangTest` or other test helpers) with 30 test methods covering `FastDateParser`:

- Constructor validation (null pattern/timeZone → NPE, null locale → default, unsupported pattern letters, unterminated quotes, invalid `X` width)
- Getters (`getPattern`, `getLocale`, `getTimeZone` defensive copy), `equals`/`hashCode`, `toString`/`toStringAll`
- Core parsing happy paths and `ParseException`/`ParsePosition` error-index behavior on mismatches, overflow, and out-of-bounds positions
- Two-digit year century adjustment boundaries, 12/24-hour wrap-around edge cases, quoted literals, day-of-week text strategy failures, week-year (`Y`) resolution, Japanese Imperial locale error messaging, and `Serializable` round-trip

All tests use Java 8-compatible syntax (anonymous classes instead of lambdas, no diamond operator) and pass via `./_tools/test.sh`, both individually and alongside the full `*AgentTest` suite.
